items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Crawford' in the context of Buddy Teeba's stepfather's name ('Buddy was Teeba. Buddy told us his name, you know. Crawford.') and later the interviewer lists 'Paul Crawford' among names on a list, but the interviewee provides no personal interaction or relationship descripti

ctx.x: But who did Buddy learn from?

Who did Buddy learn from? Who liked Buddy? I didn't know who learned Buddy. You know, that wasn't Buddy's daddy. No, stepdaddy. They say he raised Buddy from a little baby. Buddy know what he, but we always thought he was his daddy, but he wasn't. So he raised Buddy, so Buddy went by his name. Buddy was Teeba. Buddy told us his name, you know. Crawford.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] And I'm Dick Allen. My name's Paul Crawford.

ctx.x: Somebody call me Little Dad and Charlie sometimes. I'm calling him a bandit player and he's called a Little Dad.
And I'm Dick Allen. My name's Paul Crawford. Could we get your name down too, Ms. Ivor?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: I was young then, you know. He had Bab Frank. He had a good band in his days... I just remember who else he had, you know.

ctx.x: Paul Crawford. And Dick Allen. Four of us, yeah. He wanted to talk about Bab Frank. Ask him about Bab.

So he wanted to talk about Bab Frank. I'll tell you a message I know about him. I was young then, you know. He had Bab Frank. He had a good band in his days, you know. He had a 70th band. He used to play all for these lawn parties, they called him at that time, yeah. And, uh, he was good at that time. He played a piccolo. Yeah, Kutcher Martin with him. Henry Martin. And I just remember who else he had, you know. But yeah, he was strong. He and John Robeshoe were the strongest one at that time, you know. For…
